title: An iron rod through the skull changed a man

lines.text: In 1848, an iron rod shot straight through a man's skull. He survived, but his friends said he was no longer the same man.
Phineas Gage was blasting rock for a railroad in Vermont.
An explosion fired his tamping iron, over a metre long and six kilos, up through his head.
It entered under his left cheek, passed behind his eye, and exited through the top of his skull.
Within minutes, he was talking. He walked with little help.
But his doctor later wrote that his friends said he was, no longer Gage.
Historians now think some of those changes were exaggerated, and some may have faded.
He later worked as a stagecoach driver in Chile.
Gage became one of the first clues that the brain shapes who we are.

sources.claim: 13 September 1848 near Cavendish, Vermont; tamping iron 1.1 m long, 6 kg; entered left cheek, behind left eye, exited top of skull; conscious and speaking within minutes
Dr Harlow reported in 1868 that friends said he was 'no longer Gage'; later accounts exaggerated the change; he worked as a stagecoach driver in Chile
